page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates variable performance profiles. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores fall within the average range, as does software compilation with Clang and Redis SET operations, which reaches 6.25 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests scoring in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth remains average, but complex decompression tasks and medium-sized LLM inference tasks demonstrate poor performance, landing in the bottom 10%.

The t3.2xlarge utilizes a burstable CPU credit model, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads with variable or spike-prone CPU utilization rather than sustained high-compute demands. The primary tradeoff is the risk of performance throttling once CPU credits are exhausted, as reflected in its lower single-core benchmark tiers. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations with moderate transaction rates, and static web serving where continuous maximum CPU performance is not required.
